metadata.title: Sacituzumab Govitecan Therapy
metadata.indication: Adults with unresectable or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer after at least two prior systemic therapies, including at least one for advanced disease (NCCP00794a).
metadata.partial_assessment_note: Only entered values are assessed; omitted clinical domains remain explicitly unassessed.
metadata.partial_assessment_policy: Each entered value is assessed independently. Omitted domains remain unassessed and are never assumed normal.

catalogue_reconciliation.scope_note: The NCCP states that its website list is not comprehensive. This reconciliation does not assert that every possible national regimen is published online.

encoding_maturity.label: Source reconciled rule encoding · clinical/pharmacy review pending; source differences flagged
encoding_maturity.scope_note: NCCP00794 v3 and current EU SmPC safety reviewed; material differences remain explicit and require Consultant/pharmacy reconciliation.

metadata.catalogue_source_check_scope: Catalogue presence and source link structure only; not rule level source fidelity.
metadata.source_version_verification_method: Current official breast metastatic catalogue link followed; PDF downloaded directly with freshness query and header/version table checked locally; current NCCP v3 compared with EU SmPC
metadata.schedule_summary: Two treatment visits in each three-week cycle: Day 1, then Day 8. There is no planned infusion on Day 15. The next cycle starts after Day 21 if the team confirms it is appropriate.

clinical_governance.prescriptive_authority: Treatment plan must be initiated by a Consultant Medical Oncologist.
clinical_governance.dose_modification_note: Any dose modification should be discussed with a Consultant.
clinical_governance.disclaimer: Decision-support encoding of the current NCCP source. It does not replace the NCCP regimen, clinical judgement, local policy, prescribing review or pharmacy verification.

cycle_day.label: Treatment day
cycle_day.help_text: Optional. ANC below 1.0 requires a hold on either treatment day; ANC from 1.0 to below 1.5 requires the day to distinguish Day 1 from Day 8. Other entered values can be assessed without a day.

anc.label: ANC (×10⁹/L)
anc.source_grading_note: NCCP00794 v3 does not identify a CTCAE version in its dose table. This panel shows the source treatment/qualification criterion; it must not silently substitute the changed CTCAE v6 ANC or platelet grades. Agree the source grading convention with Consultant/pharmacy for grade-based historical events.
anc.assessment_guidance: NCCP treatment thresholds: Day 1 requires ANC ≥1.5 ×10⁹/L; Day 8 requires ANC ≥1.0 ×10⁹/L. These are dosing thresholds, not a numeric CTCAE grade. Review fever, duration and qualifying-event history separately.

severe_neutropenia_occurrence.label: Severe-neutropenia occurrence number
severe_neutropenia_occurrence.help_text: Qualifying episodes: grade 4 neutropenia ≥7 days (or less if clinically indicated), grade 3–4 febrile neutropenia, or grade 3–4 neutropenia delaying treatment 2–3 weeks. This is event history; current ANC and fever must still be assessed. No re-escalation after toxicity reduction.

neutropenia_delay_weeks.label: Dose delay from grade 3–4 neutropenia (weeks)
neutropenia_delay_weeks.source_grading_note: NCCP00794 v3 does not identify a CTCAE version in its dose table. This panel shows the source treatment/qualification criterion; it must not silently substitute the changed CTCAE v6 ANC or platelet grades. Agree the source grading convention with Consultant/pharmacy for grade-based historical events.
neutropenia_delay_weeks.assessment_guidance: Enter weeks of treatment delay caused by source-graded grade 3–4 neutropenia: 2–3 weeks qualifies for the occurrence pathway; beyond 3 weeks NCCP specifies discontinuation. This value is a duration, not an ANC or a CTCAE grade.

febrile_neutropenia_grade34.label: Current febrile neutropenia meeting protocol criteria
febrile_neutropenia_grade34.help_text: Assess ANC together with a single oral temperature >38.3°C, temperature ≥38.0°C sustained for more than 1 hour, and/or concurrent clinically significant infection. Treat as an urgent oncology complication.
febrile_neutropenia_grade34.source_grading_note: NCCP00794 v3 does not identify a CTCAE version in its dose table. This panel shows the source treatment/qualification criterion; it must not silently substitute the changed CTCAE v6 ANC or platelet grades. Agree the source grading convention with Consultant/pharmacy for grade-based historical events.
febrile_neutropenia_grade34.assessment_guidance: This is a clinical event flag, not a value to assign an automatic grade. Confirm neutropenic fever and assess sepsis urgently; do not administer sacituzumab during neutropenic fever. Use local urgent-care criteria, even when the historical dose-table grade has not been established.

grade4_neutropenia_days.label: Current grade 4 neutropenia duration (days)
grade4_neutropenia_days.help_text: Use for ongoing grade 4 neutropenia; enter prior resolved qualifying episodes in the severe-neutropenia occurrence field instead.
grade4_neutropenia_days.source_grading_note: NCCP00794 v3 does not identify a CTCAE version in its dose table. This panel shows the source treatment/qualification criterion; it must not silently substitute the changed CTCAE v6 ANC or platelet grades. Agree the source grading convention with Consultant/pharmacy for grade-based historical events.
grade4_neutropenia_days.assessment_guidance: Enter days of ongoing neutropenia already established as grade 4 using the source-compatible grading convention. NCCP qualifies ≥7 days, or less when clinically indicated. This duration must not be automatically graded as an ANC result; current ANC and fever still require assessment.

non_neutropenic_severe_occurrence.label: Severe non-neutropenic toxicity occurrence
non_neutropenic_severe_occurrence.help_text: Qualifying severe non-neutropenic event history per NCCP Table 1. First/second occurrence wording differs from the current EU dose ladder; reconcile the second occurrence with Consultant/pharmacy. Current toxicity and recovery must be assessed separately.

nonhaem_grade.label: Worst current non-haematological toxicity (CTCAE)

options.label: Grade 0 — no toxicity
options.description: No clinical or laboratory evidence of non-haematological toxicity.

options.label: Grade 1 — mild
options.description: Mild or asymptomatic; clinical observation or diagnostic review only; intervention generally not indicated.

options.label: Grade 2 — moderate
options.description: Moderate symptoms or abnormality; minimal, local or non-invasive intervention may be indicated; limits age-appropriate instrumental activities of daily living.

options.label: Grade 3 — severe
options.description: Severe or medically significant but not immediately life-threatening; hospitalisation or prolongation of hospitalisation may be indicated; disabling; limits self-care activities of daily living.

options.label: Grade 4 — life-threatening
options.description: Life-threatening consequences requiring urgent intervention.

nonhaem_grade.assessment_guidance: Name the exact non-haematological adverse event first and apply that event's own CTCAE v5.0 criterion. The general Grade 1-4 severity anchors are a screening aid only and are not a substitute for the named term.

uncontrolled_nvd.label: Severe nausea, vomiting or diarrhoea despite optimal treatment
uncontrolled_nvd.help_text: For diarrhoea, document stools above baseline, nocturnal stools, continence, hydration, IV fluids and admission. For nausea/vomiting, assess oral intake, weight, dehydration, IV fluids/tube feeding and hospitalisation.

not_recovered_within_3_weeks.label: Severe non-neutropenic toxicity not recovered to grade ≤1 within 3 weeks
not_recovered_within_3_weeks.help_text: NCCP Table 1 non-neutropenic haematological/non-haematological toxicity, grade 3 nausea or grade 3–4 vomiting; separate field covers neutropenia delay.
not_recovered_within_3_weeks.source_grading_note: NCCP00794 v3 does not identify a CTCAE version in its dose table. This panel shows the source treatment/qualification criterion; it must not silently substitute the changed CTCAE v6 ANC or platelet grades. Agree the source grading convention with Consultant/pharmacy for grade-based historical events.
not_recovered_within_3_weeks.assessment_guidance: Source criterion: qualifying severe non-neutropenic toxicity has not recovered to grade ≤1 within 3 weeks. Confirm the specific event and recovery history. This Yes/No input is not a new generic CTCAE grade.

prior_advanced_therapy.label: At least one prior systemic therapy for advanced disease

crcl_ml_min.label: Creatinine clearance category

options.label: 15 to <60 mL/min — NCCP no adjustment expected

renal_input.reason: NCCP Table2 splits CrCl at60; the current EU SmPC identifies absent severe/end-stage data below15. No continuous dose calculation is performed.

crcl_ml_min.assessment_guidance: Choose the category containing the verified creatinine clearance. Numerical values remain supported for existing callers; do not substitute an unverified eGFR. Dialysis requires specialist reconciliation.

gilbert_syndrome.label: Known Gilbert syndrome
gilbert_syndrome.help_text: Review bilirubin interpretation, UGT1A1 activity and toxicity risk. Do not assume all Gilbert syndrome patients have the same genotype.

increased_febrile_neutropenia_risk.label: Increased febrile-neutropenia risk
increased_febrile_neutropenia_risk.help_text: Examples: age 65 or older, previous neutropenia, poor performance status, organ dysfunction or multiple comorbidities.

ugt1a1_interacting_medicine.label: UGT1A1 inhibitor or inducer requiring review

infusion_reaction_grade.label: Infusion reaction grade

options.label: Grade 0
options.description: No infusion-related or hypersensitivity reaction.

options.label: Grade 1
options.description: Mild transient reaction; interruption of the infusion is not indicated; intervention not indicated.

options.label: Grade 2
options.description: Infusion interruption or treatment is indicated, with prompt response to symptomatic medication; prophylaxis may be needed for 24 hours or less.

options.label: Grade 3
options.description: Prolonged symptoms not rapidly responsive to treatment/brief interruption, or recurrence after initial improvement; hospitalisation indicated for clinical sequelae.

options.label: Grade 4
options.description: Life-threatening consequences; urgent intervention required.

infusion_reaction_grade.assessment_guidance: Document timing, symptoms, whether the infusion was interrupted, treatment given, speed of recovery, recurrence and any airway or haemodynamic compromise. These named CTCAE v5.0 descriptors support symptom assessment; NCCP00794 itself does not identify a CTCAE version. Apply the regimen-specific action separately.

diarrhoea_grade.label: Diarrhoea grade

options.label: Grade 0 — none
options.description: No increase above the patient's usual stool frequency or ostomy output.

options.label: Grade 1 — <4 extra stools/day
options.description: Increase of fewer than 4 stools per day above baseline, or mild increase in ostomy output.

options.label: Grade 2 — 4–6 extra stools/day
options.description: Increase of 4–6 stools per day above baseline, or moderate increase in ostomy output; limits instrumental activities of daily living.

options.label: Grade 3 — ≥7 extra stools/day, admission indicated, severe ostomy output or limited self-care
options.description: At least 7 additional stools per day above baseline; hospital admission indicated; severe increase in ostomy output; or limitation of self-care activities.

options.label: Grade 4 — life-threatening; urgent intervention
options.description: Life-threatening consequences; urgent intervention required.

diarrhoea_grade.help_text: Compare with baseline; assess hydration, blood, fever, abdominal pain, continence, IV fluids and admission. Acute cholinergic symptoms are assessed separately.
diarrhoea_grade.assessment_guidance: Count stools per day above the patient's baseline. Assess ostomy output, continence, hydration, fever, abdominal pain, sepsis and whether hospital care is indicated. These named CTCAE v5.0 descriptors support symptom assessment; NCCP00794 itself does not identify a CTCAE version. Apply the regimen-specific action separately.

nausea_grade.label: Nausea grade

options.label: Grade 0 — none
options.description: none

options.label: Grade 1 — appetite loss without altered intake
options.description: appetite loss without altered intake

options.label: Grade 2 — decreased intake without significant weight loss/dehydration
options.description: Reduced oral intake without significant weight loss, dehydration or malnutrition.

options.label: Grade 3 — inadequate intake; tube feeding, TPN or admission indicated
options.description: inadequate intake; tube feeding, TPN or admission indicated

nausea_grade.source_grading_note: Explicit named CTCAE v5.0 symptom descriptions support clinical grading. NCCP00794 itself does not specify a CTCAE version; a symptom grade is distinct from its treatment action.
nausea_grade.assessment_guidance: Assess oral intake, hydration, weight loss, need for IV fluids, nutritional support and admission. Use the named nausea/vomiting term rather than general severity anchors.

vomiting_grade.label: Vomiting grade

options.label: Grade 0 — none
options.description: none

options.label: Grade 1 — intervention not indicated
options.description: intervention not indicated

options.label: Grade 2 — outpatient IV hydration/medical intervention
options.description: outpatient IV hydration/medical intervention

options.label: Grade 3 — tube feeding, TPN or admission indicated
options.description: tube feeding, TPN or admission indicated

options.label: Grade 4 — life-threatening; urgent intervention
options.description: life-threatening; urgent intervention

vomiting_grade.source_grading_note: Explicit named CTCAE v5.0 symptom descriptions support clinical grading. NCCP00794 itself does not specify a CTCAE version; a symptom grade is distinct from its treatment action.
vomiting_grade.assessment_guidance: Assess oral intake, hydration, weight loss, need for IV fluids, nutritional support and admission. Use the named nausea/vomiting term rather than general severity anchors.

other_grade34_persisting_despite_optimal.label: Other grade 3–4 toxicity persists despite optimal management
other_grade34_persisting_despite_optimal.help_text: NCCP qualifying criterion: grade 4 of any duration, or other grade 3–4 non-haematological toxicity >48 hours despite optimal management. Current SmPC uses grade 3–4 of any duration despite optimal management. Review this difference.
other_grade34_persisting_despite_optimal.source_grading_note: NCCP00794 v3 does not identify a CTCAE version in its dose table. This panel shows the source treatment/qualification criterion; it must not silently substitute the changed CTCAE v6 ANC or platelet grades. Agree the source grading convention with Consultant/pharmacy for grade-based historical events.
other_grade34_persisting_despite_optimal.assessment_guidance: Confirm the named grade 3–4 adverse event and response to optimal management. NCCP uses >48 hours for other grade 3 non-haematological toxicity; current EU SmPC uses any duration. This Boolean records that clinical judgement and must not generate an automatic grade.

severe_non_neutropenic_delay_weeks.label: Delay due to severe non-neutropenic toxicity

cholinergic_symptoms.label: Acute cramping, diarrhoea or salivation during/soon after infusion

platelets_x10e9_l.label: Platelets — monitor / assess toxicity
platelets_x10e9_l.assessment_guidance: Monitoring value: NCCP00794 requires adequate haematology but gives no isolated numerical platelet dosing threshold. Assess bleeding, the named toxicity and clinical context. No CTCAE grade or treatment clearance is inferred from this panel.
platelets_x10e9_l.source_grading_note: NCCP00794 v3 does not identify a CTCAE version in its dose table. This panel shows the source treatment/qualification criterion; it must not silently substitute the changed CTCAE v6 ANC or platelet grades. Agree the source grading convention with Consultant/pharmacy for grade-based historical events.

hb_g_dl.label: Haemoglobin — monitor / assess toxicity
hb_g_dl.assessment_guidance: Monitoring value: NCCP00794 gives no isolated numerical haemoglobin dosing threshold. Assess anaemia symptoms, transfusion needs and the named toxicity. No treatment clearance is inferred.
hb_g_dl.source_grading_note: NCCP00794 v3 does not identify a CTCAE version in its dose table. This panel shows the source treatment/qualification criterion; it must not silently substitute the changed CTCAE v6 ANC or platelet grades. Agree the source grading convention with Consultant/pharmacy for grade-based historical events.

output_templates.proceed: No encoded contraindication or hold criterion was triggered. Complete normal prescribing and pharmacy checks.
output_templates.coverage_gap: Only entered values were assessed; unentered clinically relevant fields remain unassessed.

action.recommendation: Do not administer in known hypersensitivity to sacituzumab govitecan or excipients.

rules.explanation: Do not administer in known hypersensitivity to sacituzumab govitecan or excipients.

action.recommendation: Do not administer during pregnancy.

rules.explanation: Do not administer during pregnancy.

action.recommendation: Do not administer while breastfeeding.

rules.explanation: Do not administer while breastfeeding.

action.recommendation: Active uncontrolled infection is a NCCP caution (moved from exclusions in v2). Urgent clinical assessment and infection treatment; Consultant decides timing. This field alone is not an encoded absolute contraindication.

rules.explanation: Active uncontrolled infection is a NCCP caution (moved from exclusions in v2). Urgent clinical assessment and infection treatment; Consultant decides timing. This field alone is not an encoded absolute contraindication.

action.recommendation: Known UGT1A1*28 homozygosity increases SN-38 toxicity risk. NCCP advises considering a lower starting dose and escalation according to cycle-1 toxicity; no specific reduced starting dose is supplied. Consultant/pharmacy should agree dose and close early monitoring. Do not re-escalate a dose reduced for adverse reactions.

rules.explanation: Known UGT1A1*28 homozygosity increases SN-38 toxicity risk. NCCP advises considering a lower starting dose and escalation according to cycle-1 toxicity; no specific reduced starting dose is supplied. Consultant/pharmacy should agree dose and close early monitoring. Do not re-escalate a dose reduced for adverse reactions.

action.recommendation: Review bilirubin, genotype if already known and increased toxicity risk in Gilbert syndrome. NCCP links consideration of a lower starting dose to known UGT1A1*28 homozygosity; do not infer the genotype from Gilbert syndrome alone.

rules.explanation: Review bilirubin, genotype if already known and increased toxicity risk in Gilbert syndrome. NCCP links consideration of a lower starting dose to known UGT1A1*28 homozygosity; do not infer the genotype from Gilbert syndrome alone.

action.recommendation: Use caution with concomitant UGT1A1 inhibitors and inducers; oncology pharmacy should review potential exposure/toxicity or reduced efficacy risks. The EU SmPC does not make these combinations an absolute contraindication.

rules.explanation: Use caution with concomitant UGT1A1 inhibitors and inducers; oncology pharmacy should review potential exposure/toxicity or reduced efficacy risks. The EU SmPC does not make these combinations an absolute contraindication.

action.recommendation: Do not administer Day 1 when ANC <1.5 ×10⁹/L. Repeat count and reassess recovery and clinical state.

rules.explanation: Do not administer Day 1 when ANC <1.5 ×10⁹/L. Repeat count and reassess recovery and clinical state.

action.recommendation: Do not administer Day 8 when ANC <1.0 ×10⁹/L. Repeat count and reassess recovery and clinical state.

rules.explanation: Do not administer Day 8 when ANC <1.0 ×10⁹/L. Repeat count and reassess recovery and clinical state.

action.recommendation: ANC <1.0 ×10⁹/L is below both Day 1 and Day 8 thresholds. Withhold without requiring a treatment-day entry; review fever, infection, duration and recovery.

rules.explanation: ANC <1.0 ×10⁹/L is below both Day 1 and Day 8 thresholds. Withhold without requiring a treatment-day entry; review fever, infection, duration and recovery.

action.recommendation: ANC is between 1.0 and <1.5 ×10⁹/L: hold on Day 1; the ANC threshold alone is met on Day 8. Confirm treatment day before a dosing decision. Other entered domains remain assessable.

rules.explanation: ANC is between 1.0 and <1.5 ×10⁹/L: hold on Day 1; the ANC threshold alone is met on Day 8. Confirm treatment day before a dosing decision. Other entered domains remain assessable.

action.recommendation: Do not administer with neutropenic fever. Urgent assessment and anti-infective treatment according to local neutropenic-sepsis policy; give G-CSF as clinically indicated and review the recurrence-based dose pathway.

rules.explanation: Do not administer with neutropenic fever. Urgent assessment and anti-infective treatment according to local neutropenic-sepsis policy; give G-CSF as clinically indicated and review the recurrence-based dose pathway.

action.recommendation: Prolonged grade 4 neutropenia meets the severe-neutropenia pathway. Withhold pending recovery, administer G-CSF as clinically indicated and establish qualifying occurrence history before restart.

rules.explanation: Prolonged grade 4 neutropenia meets the severe-neutropenia pathway. Withhold pending recovery, administer G-CSF as clinically indicated and establish qualifying occurrence history before restart.

action.recommendation: A 2–3-week delay due to grade 3–4 neutropenia meets the NCCP severe-neutropenia pathway. Check occurrence history, recovery and G-CSF plan before restarting.

rules.explanation: A 2–3-week delay due to grade 3–4 neutropenia meets the NCCP severe-neutropenia pathway. Check occurrence history, recovery and G-CSF plan before restarting.

action.recommendation: NCCP Table 1: discontinue if grade 3–4 neutropenia delays recovery beyond 3 weeks; administer G-CSF as clinically indicated. The current EU SmPC uses a recurrence/dose-level approach; Consultant/pharmacy must reconcile before any rechallenge.

rules.explanation: NCCP Table 1: discontinue if grade 3–4 neutropenia delays recovery beyond 3 weeks; administer G-CSF as clinically indicated. The current EU SmPC uses a recurrence/dose-level approach; Consultant/pharmacy must reconcile before any rechallenge.

action.recommendation: First qualifying severe-neutropenia event: NCCP specifies G-CSF as soon as clinically indicated. Current ANC, infection and recovery determine withholding/restart; this history alone does not clear the current dose.

rules.explanation: First qualifying severe-neutropenia event: NCCP specifies G-CSF as soon as clinically indicated. Current ANC, infection and recovery determine withholding/restart; this history alone does not clear the current dose.

action.recommendation: Second qualifying severe-neutropenia event: NCCP 25% reduction from the original 10 mg/kg gives 7.5 mg/kg, with G-CSF. Restart only after the appropriate Day 1/Day 8 ANC recovery and resolution of neutropenic fever; no re-escalation.

rules.explanation: Second qualifying severe-neutropenia event: NCCP 25% reduction from the original 10 mg/kg gives 7.5 mg/kg, with G-CSF. Restart only after the appropriate Day 1/Day 8 ANC recovery and resolution of neutropenic fever; no re-escalation.

action.recommendation: Third qualifying severe-neutropenia event: NCCP 50% reduction from the original 10 mg/kg gives 5 mg/kg, with G-CSF. Restart only after the appropriate ANC recovery and resolution of neutropenic fever; no re-escalation.

rules.explanation: Third qualifying severe-neutropenia event: NCCP 50% reduction from the original 10 mg/kg gives 5 mg/kg, with G-CSF. Restart only after the appropriate ANC recovery and resolution of neutropenic fever; no re-escalation.

action.recommendation: Fourth qualifying severe-neutropenia event: discontinue and administer G-CSF as clinically indicated.

rules.explanation: Fourth qualifying severe-neutropenia event: discontinue and administer G-CSF as clinically indicated.

action.recommendation: After recovery from the first qualifying severe non-neutropenic event, NCCP specifies a 25% reduction (7.5 mg/kg from 10 mg/kg). Do not administer while current severe toxicity persists.

rules.explanation: After recovery from the first qualifying severe non-neutropenic event, NCCP specifies a 25% reduction (7.5 mg/kg from 10 mg/kg). Do not administer while current severe toxicity persists.

action.recommendation: Source conflict: NCCP Table 1 repeats “25% dose reduction” for the second severe non-neutropenic occurrence; the current EU SmPC explicitly steps 10 → 7.5 → 5 mg/kg. Consultant/pharmacy must resolve the intended dose. No automatic repeated percentage or numeric restart dose is supplied.

rules.explanation: Source conflict: NCCP Table 1 repeats “25% dose reduction” for the second severe non-neutropenic occurrence; the current EU SmPC explicitly steps 10 → 7.5 → 5 mg/kg. Consultant/pharmacy must resolve the intended dose. No automatic repeated percentage or numeric restart dose is supplied.

action.recommendation: Third qualifying severe non-neutropenic event: discontinue treatment.

rules.explanation: Third qualifying severe non-neutropenic event: discontinue treatment.

action.recommendation: NCCP Table 1: discontinue qualifying severe non-neutropenic toxicity that fails to recover to grade ≤1 within 3 weeks. Reconcile the differing current EU dose-level algorithm before considering any rechallenge.

rules.explanation: NCCP Table 1: discontinue qualifying severe non-neutropenic toxicity that fails to recover to grade ≤1 within 3 weeks. Reconcile the differing current EU dose-level algorithm before considering any rechallenge.

action.recommendation: A 2–3-week delay due to severe non-neutropenic toxicity meets the NCCP occurrence-based reduction pathway; confirm recovery and occurrence before selecting a dose.

rules.explanation: A 2–3-week delay due to severe non-neutropenic toxicity meets the NCCP occurrence-based reduction pathway; confirm recovery and occurrence before selecting a dose.

action.recommendation: NCCP Table 1: discontinue qualifying severe non-neutropenic toxicity with recovery delayed beyond 3 weeks; Consultant/pharmacy reconcile with current EU SmPC before any rechallenge.

rules.explanation: NCCP Table 1: discontinue qualifying severe non-neutropenic toxicity with recovery delayed beyond 3 weeks; Consultant/pharmacy reconcile with current EU SmPC before any rechallenge.

action.recommendation: Withhold for grade 3–4 nausea, vomiting or diarrhoea despite optimal treatment; treat the cause and dehydration, and wait for recovery to grade ≤1. Then apply the occurrence-based pathway with source reconciliation for the second event.

rules.explanation: Withhold for grade 3–4 nausea, vomiting or diarrhoea despite optimal treatment; treat the cause and dehydration, and wait for recovery to grade ≤1. Then apply the occurrence-based pathway with source reconciliation for the second event.

action.recommendation: Do not administer with grade 3–4 diarrhoea. Assess infection, hydration and electrolytes; treat promptly. Resume only after resolution to grade ≤1 with the appropriate dose review.

rules.explanation: Do not administer with grade 3–4 diarrhoea. Assess infection, hydration and electrolytes; treat promptly. Resume only after resolution to grade ≤1 with the appropriate dose review.

action.recommendation: Do not administer with grade 3 nausea; optimise antiemetics and hydration. Resume only after recovery to grade ≤1 and review the required dose modification.

rules.explanation: Do not administer with grade 3 nausea; optimise antiemetics and hydration. Resume only after recovery to grade ≤1 and review the required dose modification.

action.recommendation: Do not administer with grade 3–4 vomiting; optimise antiemetics and hydration. Resume only after recovery to grade ≤1 and review the required dose modification.

rules.explanation: Do not administer with grade 3–4 vomiting; optimise antiemetics and hydration. Resume only after recovery to grade ≤1 and review the required dose modification.

action.recommendation: Grade 4 non-haematological toxicity of any duration qualifies for interruption and the severe-toxicity pathway. Urgent assessment; do not administer until recovery and Consultant review.

rules.explanation: Grade 4 non-haematological toxicity of any duration qualifies for interruption and the severe-toxicity pathway. Urgent assessment; do not administer until recovery and Consultant review.

action.recommendation: Identify the specific grade 3 event, duration and response to management. NCCP qualifying criteria and current EU SmPC differ for other grade 3 toxicity; do not select an automatic dose from a generic grade alone.

rules.explanation: Identify the specific grade 3 event, duration and response to management. NCCP qualifying criteria and current EU SmPC differ for other grade 3 toxicity; do not select an automatic dose from a generic grade alone.

action.recommendation: Withhold persistent grade 3–4 toxicity despite optimal medical management until recovery to grade ≤1, then review the event-specific dose ladder. NCCP uses a >48-hour threshold for other grade 3 non-haematological toxicity; current EU SmPC uses any duration.

rules.explanation: Withhold persistent grade 3–4 toxicity despite optimal medical management until recovery to grade ≤1, then review the event-specific dose ladder. NCCP uses a >48-hour threshold for other grade 3 non-haematological toxicity; current EU SmPC uses any duration.

action.recommendation: Slow or interrupt the infusion and manage the reaction with the clinical team. Subsequent infusion decisions require recovery and review; this does not mandate permanent discontinuation for every grade 1–3 reaction.

rules.explanation: Slow or interrupt the infusion and manage the reaction with the clinical team. Subsequent infusion decisions require recovery and review; this does not mandate permanent discontinuation for every grade 1–3 reaction.

action.recommendation: Permanently discontinue for life-threatening / grade 4 infusion reaction; initiate emergency treatment.

rules.explanation: Permanently discontinue for life-threatening / grade 4 infusion reaction; initiate emergency treatment.

action.recommendation: Source conflict: NCCP Table 2 says no adjustment is expected in moderate/severe hepatic impairment, whereas the current EU SmPC states safety is unestablished and use should be avoided above its bilirubin/transaminase limits. Consultant/pharmacy must reconcile; do not infer safe full-dose treatment.

rules.explanation: Source conflict: NCCP Table 2 says no adjustment is expected in moderate/severe hepatic impairment, whereas the current EU SmPC states safety is unestablished and use should be avoided above its bilirubin/transaminase limits. Consultant/pharmacy must reconcile; do not infer safe full-dose treatment.

action.recommendation: Bilirubin >1.5 ×ULN: current EU SmPC advises avoiding use; do not administer pending Consultant/pharmacy review. This differs from NCCP Table 2’s no-adjustment-expected wording for moderate/severe impairment.

rules.explanation: Bilirubin >1.5 ×ULN: current EU SmPC advises avoiding use; do not administer pending Consultant/pharmacy review. This differs from NCCP Table 2’s no-adjustment-expected wording for moderate/severe impairment.

action.recommendation: AST/ALT >3 ×ULN without liver metastases: current EU SmPC advises avoiding use. Withhold pending Consultant/pharmacy reconciliation with NCCP Table 2.

rules.explanation: AST/ALT >3 ×ULN without liver metastases: current EU SmPC advises avoiding use. Withhold pending Consultant/pharmacy reconciliation with NCCP Table 2.

action.recommendation: AST/ALT >5 ×ULN exceeds the current EU SmPC studied limits with or without liver metastases. Withhold pending Consultant/pharmacy review.

rules.explanation: AST/ALT >5 ×ULN exceeds the current EU SmPC studied limits with or without liver metastases. Withhold pending Consultant/pharmacy review.

action.recommendation: AST/ALT is >3 to ≤5 ×ULN. Confirm liver-metastasis status: the EU SmPC avoidance threshold is >3 without and >5 with liver metastases. Missing context is not assumed normal.

rules.explanation: AST/ALT is >3 to ≤5 ×ULN. Confirm liver-metastasis status: the EU SmPC avoidance threshold is >3 without and >5 with liver metastases. Missing context is not assumed normal.

action.recommendation: CrCl <15 mL/min: current EU SmPC reports no study data in this severe/end-stage range. NCCP says no adjustment is expected; reconcile with Consultant/pharmacy before treatment rather than treating the absence of a dose reduction as proof of safety.

rules.explanation: CrCl <15 mL/min: current EU SmPC reports no study data in this severe/end-stage range. NCCP says no adjustment is expected; reconcile with Consultant/pharmacy before treatment rather than treating the absence of a dose reduction as proof of safety.

action.recommendation: NCCP Table 2 states no renal dose adjustment is expected below CrCl 60 mL/min. Assess renal function and clinical status; current EU SmPC describes no starting-dose adjustment for mild/moderate impairment. This is not overall treatment clearance.

supportive_care.supportive_medications_label: NCCP antiemetic guidance for high emetogenic risk
premedication_summary: High emetic risk: reconcile high-risk prophylaxis with local/NCIS protocol before BOTH Day 1 and Day 8 doses.
NCCP suggested infusion premedication: paracetamol 1 g PO 60 minutes; chlorphenamine 10 mg IV, famotidine 20 mg IV and dexamethasone 12 mg PO 30 minutes before infusion.
Dexamethasone used for infusion-reaction prevention also contributes antiemetic cover; reconcile the total steroid dose to avoid duplication.
other_supportive_care: Consider primary G-CSF from cycle1 in increased-risk patients; secondary prophylaxis/treatment based on neutropenia and Consultant/pharmacy-approved schedule.

Provide a written diarrhoea action plan and take-home antiemetics; assess infection, hydration and electrolyte loss promptly. NCCP high-dose loperamide instructions require a locally approved prescription, not unsupervised generic dosing.
Observe during each infusion and for ≥30 minutes afterwards.
For excessive cholinergic symptoms, consider atropine on later infusions; NCCP excludes atropine in glaucoma.
supportive_care.mapping_basis: The active ADC is high emetogenic risk in NCCP V6 Table 7.

ctcae_standard.reference: CTCAE grading as cited by the NCCP source protocol
ctcae_standard.display_requirement: Every grade-based input includes toxicity-specific criteria and practical assessment guidance. Do not select a grade from the number alone.

indications.description: Adults with unresectable or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer after at least two prior systemic therapies, including at least one for advanced disease (NCCP00794a).

administration.notes: First infusion over 3 hours; subsequent infusions 1–2 hours if tolerated. Observe during and for at least 30 minutes after each infusion. Continue until progression or unacceptable toxicity.

baseline: FBC, renal and liver profile; glucose, electrolytes, magnesium, calcium and phosphate (NCCP p2).
Pregnancy test where relevant. ECG only if clinically indicated. Assess infection, UGT1A1 history and individual febrile-neutropenia risk.
regular: FBC, renal and liver profile before each cycle; ANC must also be checked against the separate Day 8 dosing threshold (NCCP p2 / EU SmPC4.4).
Glucose, electrolytes, magnesium, calcium and phosphate every second cycle (NCCP p2).
Pregnancy testing before each cycle where relevant; ECG only if clinically indicated.
Review bowel symptoms, hydration, oral intake, fever and infection before each infusion; observe during and ≥30 minutes after each infusion.
monitoring.early: Fatal infections in neutropenia have occurred particularly in the first two cycles; consider primary G-CSF from cycle 1 for increased-risk patients (EU SmPC4.4).
monitoring.disease: Response scans and other tests follow the Consultant treatment plan. NCCP does not specify a universal CT, tumour-marker or MRI interval.
monitoring.not_routine: Routine echo, fixed ECG schedules and bone-density scanning are not drug-specific requirements for this regimen. Add tests for symptoms, comorbidity or other treatments.

source_discrepancies.nccp: Table1 repeats 25% reduction for both first and second event.
source_discrepancies.supplemental_source: EU SmPC uses explicit 10→7.5→5 mg/kg; second-event automatic dosing suppressed pending Consultant/pharmacy reconciliation.

source_discrepancies.nccp: Table2 predicts no adjustment even for moderate/severe hepatic dysfunction and dialysis.
source_discrepancies.supplemental_source: EU SmPC advises avoidance beyond bilirubin/AST/ALT bands and notes absent severe/end-stage renal data. Abnormal hepatic bands withhold; unresolved renal/dialysis cases require review.

source_discrepancies.nccp: Other grade3 toxicity >48h despite optimal management and recovery-delay >3wk discontinuation.
source_discrepancies.supplemental_source: Current EU SmPC uses grade3–4 of any duration despite optimal management and dose-level recurrences. Explicit reconciliation before any restart/rechallenge.
Broader current EU indications do not automatically establish NCCP eligibility or HSE reimbursement.
